LESSON: MATCHING AND PAIRING

Grade: PP1
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: CLASSIFICATION
Topic 1.2: Matching and Pairing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Matching and Pairing. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify similarities among 8 lessons
2. identify differences among objects in the environment
3. match similar objects in the environment
4. pair objects according to specific criteria e) appreciate the use of different objects in the environment learners match and pair objects according to likeness, sameness or use in the environment. poems on relationship or use of objects from the environment. according to one attribute using ICT devices.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify similarities among 8 lessons
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to identify similarities among 8 lessons. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. identify differences among objects in the environment
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to identify differences among objects in the environment. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. match similar objects in the environment
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to match similar objects in the environment. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

4. pair objects according to specific criteria e) appreciate the use of different objects in the environment learners match and pair objects according to likeness, sameness or use in the environment. poems on relationship or use of objects from the environment. according to one attribute using ICT devices.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to pair objects according to specific criteria e) appreciate the use of different objects in the environment learners match and pair objects according to likeness, sameness or use in the environment. poems on relationship or use of objects from the environment. according to one attribute using ICT devices. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market in your county, count 10 mangoes. Put them in 2 groups of 5. That is sorting and grouping.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row. Write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and your parent gives you 5 more, you have 12 shillings. That is addition.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Matching and Pairing.
2. Explain Matching and Pairing to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Matching and Pairing.
4. Show that you can: identify similarities among 8 lessons
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Matching and Pairing. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Matching and Pairing important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. identify similarities among 8 lessons
2. identify differences among objects in the environment
3. match similar objects in the environment
4. pair objects according to specific criteria e) appreciate the use of different objects in the environment learners match and pair objects according to likeness, sameness or use in the environment. poems on relationship or use of objects from the environment. according to one attribute using ICT devices.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
